en.headline: Hong Kong Disneyland reports theft of 17000 ticket QR codes and suspends online sales
en.dek: Police are investigating the case as access to a computer with criminal or dishonest intent after an IT worker found anomalies in the system.
body: Hong Kong Disneyland Resort has reported the theft of about 17,000 ticket QR codes from its online ticketing system and suspended sales through its website, according to reports citing sources familiar with the matter.

An IT worker at the Lantau amusement park detected unusual activity in the computer system and discovered the codes had been taken, prompting the resort to halt online ticket and hotel bookings while enhancing verification procedures at the gates.

Police have classified the case as access to a computer with a criminal or dishonest intent and the Lantau district crime squad is investigating. The resort said it would notify the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data and advised guests to buy tickets only through official channels or authorised agents to avoid losses.

The resort earlier announced it had found a cyber incident and taken protective measures, strongly recommending that visitors purchase tickets directly from official sources rather than unreliable sellers.

zh.headline: 香港迪士尼樂園報告1.7萬個門票二維碼被盜 暫停網上售票
zh.dek: 警方正以有犯罪或不誠實意圖而取用電腦調查，一名資訊科技人員發現系統異常後揭發事件。
body: 據消息指，香港迪士尼樂園度假區向警方報案，稱其網上售票系統約1.7萬個門票二維碼被盜，並已暫停官網售票及酒店預訂服務。
樂園一名負責內部系統的資訊科技人員發現電腦異常活動，隨即揭發二維碼被取走，園方即時停止網上票務運作，並加強入場時的門票核實程序。
警方將案件列為有犯罪或不誠實意圖而取用電腦，交由大嶼山警區重案組跟進。樂園表示將盡快通知個人資料私隱專員公署，並呼籲賓客只透過官方渠道或合作旅行社購買門票，以免蒙受損失。
園方較早前已公布發現網絡事件，並採取跟進及防護措施，強烈建議訪客切勿向不可靠賣家購票。
